title: Two inspection teams share the jobs

blocks.text: A water utility has inspection teams that can each do any job, one job at a time. Some teams are away on some days, given as `(first_day, last_day)` pairs, both days included. Days are numbered from 0.

Write `split_work(jobs, teams, away, horizon)` in `teams.py`. `jobs` maps a job to its days of work, `teams` lists the team names, `away` maps a team to its absences (a team with none may be missing from it), and all work must end by day `horizon`. Return, for each job, the pair `(team, start_day)`, chosen so that the last job ends as early as possible.
The model, with $`J`$ the jobs, $`d_j`$ their days, $`T`$ the teams, $`A_t`$ team $`t`$'s absences with first and last days $`f_a`$ and $`l_a`$, and $`H`$ the horizon:

The interval "present iff $`x_{j,t} = 1`$" is an optional interval with presence literal $`x_{j,t}`$; job $`j`$ has one per team, all on the same $`s_j`$. The tests check the plan you return and how early it ends, so any optimal plan passes. About twenty lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


def split_work(jobs: dict[str, int], teams: list[str], away: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]],
               horizon: int) -> dict[str, tuple[str, int]]:
    """(team, start day) for each job, so the last job ends as early as possible."""
    # TODO: a start per job, a Boolean and an optional interval per job and team, exactly one team
    # per job, a NoOverlap per team with its absences, and minimize the latest end.
    # Every pair below is a placeholder.
    return {j: ("nobody", -1) for j in jobs}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(split_work({"main_st": 3, "mill_rd": 2, "dam": 4}, ["red", "blue"], {"blue": [(0, 1)]}, 20))

cases.says: every job is given to one of the listed teams, with a whole-number start day
with one team, the jobs run one after another and end as early as possible
two teams work on different jobs at the same time, so the work ends sooner than with one team
days one team is away are blocked for that team only

origin.section: Optional Intervals Let a Job Choose Its Crew

concepts: one optional interval per crew with exactly one present lets a job choose its crew
